subject: math
title: Grade 9 Multiplying and Dividing Polynomials by a Monomial
seo_title: Grade 9 Multiplying and Dividing Polynomials Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Operations with polynomials, of degree less than or equal to 2
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 math worksheets on multiplying and dividing polynomials for the BC curriculum: multiplying monomials, the distributive property, area models, dividing a polynomial by a monomial, and area word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Multiply or divide every term: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12, and (6x² + 9x) ÷ 3x = 2x + 3.
key_sub: Multiply the coefficients and the variables: 2x × 3x = 6x², not 6x. Check a quotient by multiplying it back.
body_html:
Multiply monomials

To multiply monomials, multiply the coefficients, then multiply the variables. x × x = x2, because x2 means x times itself. Use integer rules for the signs.

ProductCoefficientsVariablesResult
(2x)(3x)2 × 3 = 6x × x = x26x2
(−5n)(−4n)(−5)(−4) = 20n × n = n220n2
4 × 5x4 × 5 = 20x20x

Multiply a monomial by a binomial

Use the distributive property: multiply the monomial by every term in the brackets. An area model shows why: the side times each part of the top gives one cell, and the cells add up to the whole area.

Example 1

Expand −3x(2x − 5).

−3x × 2x = −6x2. −3x × (−5) = 15x, because negative × negative is positive.

Answer: −6x2 + 15x

Divide a polynomial by a monomial

Divide every term by the monomial. Divide the coefficients, then the variables: x2 ÷ x = x and x ÷ x = 1. Check by multiplying the quotient by the monomial.

Example 2

Divide: 14x2 − 7x7x

14x2 ÷ 7x = 2x. −7x ÷ 7x = −1. Check: 7x(2x − 1) = 14x2 − 7x.

Answer: 2x − 1

Area problems

The area of a rectangle is length × width, so a rectangle 2x m wide and (x + 5) m long has an area of 2x(x + 5) = 2x2 + 10x m². To find a missing side, divide the area by the side you know.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3(x + 4) = 3x + 4Multiply every term: 3x + 12
2x × 3x = 6xx × x = x2, so 6x2
2x × 3x = 5x2Multiply the coefficients, do not add them
−2(x − 5) = −2x − 10−2 × (−5) = +10, so −2x + 10
(6x2 + 9x) ÷ 3x = 2x + 9Divide every term: 2x + 3
7x ÷ 7x = 0A non-zero term divided by itself is 1
Using the perimeter for an areaArea is length × width

faq.q: Do BC Grade 9 students multiply and divide polynomials?
faq.a: Yes. The Mathematics 9 Patterning standard covers operations with polynomials of degree 2 or less, which includes multiplying and dividing a polynomial by a monomial, such as 3x(2x − 5) = 6x² − 15x.

faq.q: Why is 2x × 3x equal to 6x² and not 6x?
faq.a: Multiply the numbers (2 × 3 = 6) and the variables (x × x = x²). 6x would be correct only if one of the factors had no x.

faq.q: How do you use the distributive property with a monomial?
faq.a: Multiply the monomial by every term in the brackets. For 3(x + 4), 3 × x = 3x and 3 × 4 = 12, so the answer is 3x + 12, not 3x + 4.

faq.q: How do you divide a polynomial by a monomial?
faq.a: Divide each term by the monomial. For (6x² + 9x) ÷ 3x, 6x² ÷ 3x = 2x and 9x ÷ 3x = 3, so the quotient is 2x + 3. Multiply 3x(2x + 3) to check.

items.e: Multiply the numbers and keep the variable: 4 × 5 = 20, so 4 × 5x = 20x. (9x adds 4 and 5.)
−3 × 6 = −18, so the answer is −18x. (3x adds −3 and 6. −18 drops the variable.)
A negative times a negative is positive: (−2)(−7) = 14, so the answer is 14y. (−9y adds the numbers.)
x × x means x times itself, which is x2. (2x is x + x, which is adding, not multiplying.)
Multiply the coefficients: 2 × 3 = 6. Multiply the variables: x × x = x2. So (2x)(3x) = 6x2. (6x forgets that x × x = x2. 5x2 adds 2 and 3.)
4 × 5 = 20 and x × x = x2, so the answer is 20x2. (20x forgets the second x. 9x2 adds 4 and 5.)
−3 × 2 = −6 and x × x = x2, so the answer is −6x2. (−x2 adds −3 and 2.)
(−5)(−4) = 20, because negative × negative is positive. n × n = n2, so the answer is 20n2. (−20n2 is a sign error.)
−x means −1x. 7 × (−1) = −7 and x × x = x2, so the answer is −7x2. (6x2 adds 7 and −1.)
(−1)(−1) = 1 and x × x = x2, so (−x)(−x) = x2. (−x2 is a sign error. −2x adds the terms.)
0.5 × 8 = 4 and x × x = x2, so the answer is 4x2. (8.5x2 adds. 16x2 divides 8 by 0.5.)
Multiply the coefficients: 3 × (−4) = −12. The x2 stays, so the answer is −12x2. (−12x loses the square. −x2 adds 3 and −4.)
Numbers: 2 × (−4) = −8. Variables: x × x = x2. The product is −8x2. (−8x misses one x.)
(3x)2 = (3x)(3x): 3 × 3 = 9 and x × x = x2, so 9x2. (3x2 squares only the x. 6x2 doubles the 3.)
(−2x)2 = (−2x)(−2x): (−2)(−2) = 4 and x × x = x2, so 4x2. (−4x2 forgets that negative × negative is positive.)
(3x)(4x): 3 × 4 = 12 and x × x = x2. ((3x)(4) = 12x. (6x)(6x) = 36x2. (5x)(7x) = 35x2: 5 + 7 = 12, but the coefficients must be multiplied.)

items.q: What monomial goes in the box? 4x × ☐ = 20x2
items.e: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, and x × x = x2, so the box needs 5x. Check: (4x)(5x) = 20x2. (5 gives only 20x. 16x subtracts 4 from 20.)

items.q: What monomial goes in the box? ☐ × (−3x) = 18x2
items.e: 18 ÷ (−3) = −6, and x × x = x2, so the box needs −6x. Check: (−6x)(−3x) = 18x2. (6x gives −18x2.)

items.q: Owen says (4x)(2x) = 8x. To test it, he uses x = 3. What is the value of (4x)(2x) when x = 3?
items.e: 4x = 12 and 2x = 6, so 12 × 6 = 72. But 8x = 24, so Owen is wrong: the product is 8x2 = 8 × 9 = 72. (24 uses Owen’s 8x. 54 uses 6x2.)
Multiply first: (−5x)(2x) = −10x2. Then combine like terms: −10x2 + 4x2 = −6x2. (−10x2 forgets the 4x2. −14x2 subtracts 4.)

sets.title: Multiply a monomial by a binomial

items.e: Multiply both terms by 3: 3 × x = 3x and 3 × 4 = 12. So 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12. (3x + 4 multiplies only the first term.)
5 × 2x = 10x and 5 × (−3) = −15. So the answer is 10x − 15. (10x − 3 multiplies only the first term.)
−2 × x = −2x and −2 × 6 = −12. So the answer is −2x − 12. (−2x + 12 forgets that −2 × 6 is negative.)
−4 × 3x = −12x and −4 × (−5) = 20. So the answer is −12x + 20. (−12x − 20 forgets that negative × negative is positive.)
−(x − 7) means −1 × (x − 7): −1 × x = −x and −1 × (−7) = 7. So the answer is −x + 7. (−x − 7 changes the sign of the first term only.)
x × x = x2 and x × 3 = 3x. So x(x + 3) = x2 + 3x. (x2 + 3 multiplies only the first term. 4x2 joins unlike terms.)
2x × x = 2x2 and 2x × (−5) = −10x. So the answer is 2x2 − 10x. (2x2 − 5 multiplies only the first term.)
3x × 2x = 6x2 and 3x × 4 = 12x. So the answer is 6x2 + 12x. (5x2 + 7x adds instead of multiplying.)
−x × x = −x2 and −x × (−8) = 8x. So the answer is −x2 + 8x. (−x2 − 8x forgets that negative × negative is positive.)
−3x × 2x = −6x2 and −3x × 1 = −3x. So the answer is −6x2 − 3x. (−6x2 + 1 multiplies only the first term.)
4x × 5 = 20x and 4x × (−x) = −4x2. So the answer is 20x − 4x2. (20x − x multiplies only the first term.)
−5x × (−2x) = 10x2 and −5x × 3 = −15x. So the answer is 10x2 − 15x. (10x2 + 15x gets the sign of the second term wrong.)
Multiply all three terms by 2: 2x2, −6x and 8. The answer is 2x2 − 6x + 8. (2x2 − 6x + 4 forgets the last term.)
Multiply all three terms by −3: −6x2, −3x and +15. The answer is −6x2 − 3x + 15. (−15 forgets that −3 × (−5) is positive.)
Multiplying by 12 halves each term: 4x ÷ 2 = 2x and 6 ÷ 2 = 3. The answer is 2x + 3. (2x + 6 halves only the first term. 8x + 12 doubles instead.)
Expand first: 2(x + 3) = 2x + 6. Then 2x + 6 + 4x = 6x + 6. (6x + 3 forgets to multiply 3 by 2. 12x joins unlike terms.)
Expand first: x(x + 5) = x2 + 5x. Then 5x − 2x = 3x, so the answer is x2 + 3x. (x2 − 2x + 5 multiplies only the first term.)

items.q: Ji-woo wrote 4(x + 5) = 4x + 5. What mistake did she make?
items.e: The 4 multiplies every term in the brackets: 4(x + 5) = 4x + 20. Ji-woo multiplied only the first term.
−2x × 3 = −6x and −2x × (−x) = 2x2. The answer is −6x + 2x2, which can also be written 2x2 − 6x. (−6x − 2x2 forgets that negative × negative is positive.)

items.q: Which multiplication does the area model show?
items.e: The side is 3 and the top is x + 2, so the area is 3(x + 2). (3x + 2 multiplies only the x. 2(x + 3) swaps the 2 and the 3. 3 + (x + 2) adds instead of multiplying.)

items.q: Which expression gives the total area of the model?
items.e: Area = side × top = x(x + 5), which expands to x2 + 5x. (x2 + 5 multiplies only the x.)

items.q: What is the total area of the model?
items.e: The two cells are 2 × x = 2x and 2 × 5 = 10. The total area is 2x + 10. (2x + 5 forgets to multiply 5 by 2.)

items.q: What is the total area of the model?
items.e: The cells are x × x = x2 and x × 4 = 4x. The total area is x2 + 4x. (2x + 4 adds x + x.)

items.q: What is the total area of the model?
items.e: The cells are 2x × x = 2x2 and 2x × 3 = 6x. The total area is 2x2 + 6x. (8x2 joins unlike terms.)

items.q: What is the total area of the model?
items.e: The cells are 3x × 2x = 6x2 and 3x × 1 = 3x. The total area is 6x2 + 3x. (6x2 + 1 multiplies only the first cell.)

items.q: What goes in the yellow cell of the area model?
items.e: The yellow cell is side × top: 4 × 6 = 24. (10 adds 4 and 6. 24x adds a variable that is not there.)

items.q: What goes in the yellow cell of the area model?
items.e: The yellow cell is 2x × 7 = 14x. (9x adds. 14 forgets the x.)

items.q: What goes in the yellow cell of the area model?
items.e: The yellow cell is x × 3x = 3x2. (3x forgets that x × x = x2.)

items.q: What goes in the yellow cell of the area model?
items.e: The yellow cell is −2x × 5 = −10x. (10x loses the negative sign. 3x adds −2 and 5.)

items.q: What goes in the yellow cell of the area model?
items.e: The yellow cell is 3 × (−4x) = −12x. (12x loses the negative sign. −x adds 3 and −4.)

items.q: What is the missing side length of the area model?
items.e: The side times x gives 4x2, so the side is 4x. Check: 4x × 3 = 12x. (4 would give only 4x in the first cell.)

items.q: What is the missing side length of the area model?
items.e: The side times x gives 2x, so the side is 2. Check: 2 × 5 = 10. (2x would give 2x2 in the first cell.)

items.q: What is the missing side length of the area model?
items.e: The side times x gives −3x2, so the side is −3x. Check: −3x × (−6) = 18x. (3x gives the wrong signs.)

items.q: Which binomial is missing along the top of the area model?
items.e: Divide each cell by the side 3x: 6x2 ÷ 3x = 2x and 15x ÷ 3x = 5. The top is 2x + 5. (2x + 15 divides only the first cell.)

items.q: Which binomial is missing along the top of the area model?
items.e: Divide each cell by 5x: 10x2 ÷ 5x = 2x and −20x ÷ 5x = −4. The top is 2x − 4. (2x + 4 loses the negative sign.)

items.q: What is the total area of the model?
items.e: Multiply each part by 2: 2x2, 6x and −2. The total is 2x2 + 6x − 2. (2x2 + 6x − 1 forgets the last cell.)

items.q: What is the total area of the model?
items.e: The cells are −x × x = −x2 and −x × 4 = −4x. The total is −x2 − 4x. (−x2 − 4 forgets the x in the second cell.)

items.q: What is the total area of the model?
items.e: Multiply each part by −3: −3x2, −3 × (−2x) = 6x and −3 × 5 = −15. The total is −3x2 + 6x − 15. (−3x2 − 6x − 15 forgets that negative × negative is positive.)

items.q: Arjun filled in this area model for 4x(x − 3). One cell is wrong. What should the second cell be?
items.e: The second cell is 4x × (−3) = −12x. Arjun forgot to multiply by the x in 4x. (12x loses the negative sign.)

sets.title: Divide a polynomial by a monomial

items.e: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 and x2 ÷ x = x, so the quotient is 4x. Check: (3x)(4x) = 12x2. (4x2 forgets to divide the variable. 9x subtracts.)
20 ÷ 5 = 4 and the x stays, so the quotient is 4x. (4 drops the x. 100x multiplies.)
15 ÷ 5 = 3 and x ÷ x = 1, so the quotient is 3. Check: (5x)(3) = 15x. (3x forgets that x ÷ x = 1.)
−18 ÷ 6 = −3 and x2 ÷ x = x, so the quotient is −3x. (3x loses the negative sign.)
−24 ÷ (−8) = 3, because negative ÷ negative is positive. x2 ÷ x = x, so the quotient is 3x.
7 ÷ 7 = 1 and x2 ÷ x = x, so the quotient is 1x = x. (1 cancels every x.)
Divide each term by 4: 8x ÷ 4 = 2x and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. The quotient is 2x + 3. (2x + 12 divides only the first term.)
Divide each term by 5: 10x ÷ 5 = 2x and −15 ÷ 5 = −3. The quotient is 2x − 3. (5x − 10 subtracts 5 instead of dividing.)
Divide each term by 3x: 6x2 ÷ 3x = 2x and 9x ÷ 3x = 3. The quotient is 2x + 3. (2x + 9 divides only the first term. 2x2 + 3x divides only the numbers.)
14x2 ÷ 7x = 2x and −7x ÷ 7x = −1. The quotient is 2x − 1. (2x treats 7x ÷ 7x as 0, but any non-zero term divided by itself is 1.)
−12x2 ÷ 4x = −3x and 8x ÷ 4x = 2. The quotient is −3x + 2. (−3x + 8 divides only the first term.)
Divide each term by −4x: 12x2 ÷ (−4x) = −3x and −8x ÷ (−4x) = 2. The quotient is −3x + 2. (−3x − 2 forgets that negative ÷ negative is positive.)
x2 ÷ x = x and −4x ÷ x = −4. The quotient is x − 4. (x − 4x divides only the first term.)
Divide all three terms by 3: 3x2, 2x and −1. The quotient is 3x2 + 2x − 1. (3x2 + 2x treats −3 ÷ 3 as 0.)
Divide all three terms by 2: 2x2, −4x and 1. The quotient is 2x2 − 4x + 1. (2x2 − 8x + 2 divides only the first term.)
Divide all three terms by −3: −6x2 ÷ (−3) = 2x2, 3x ÷ (−3) = −x and −9 ÷ (−3) = 3. The quotient is 2x2 − x + 3. (−2x2 + x − 3 divides by +3.)

items.q: What binomial goes in the box? 4x × ☐ = 12x2 − 20x
items.e: Divide each term by 4x: 12x2 ÷ 4x = 3x and −20x ÷ 4x = −5. The box is 3x − 5. Check: 4x(3x − 5) = 12x2 − 20x.

items.q: Simran says (8x2 + 4x) ÷ 4x = 2x. She checks by multiplying 4x by 2x and gets only 8x2. What is the correct quotient?
items.e: 8x2 ÷ 4x = 2x and 4x ÷ 4x = 1, so the quotient is 2x + 1. Check: 4x(2x + 1) = 8x2 + 4x. Simran treated 4x ÷ 4x as 0.

items.q: A school garden in Surrey is (x + 6) m long and 4 m wide. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
items.e: Area = length × width = 4(x + 6) = 4x + 24. (4x + 6 multiplies only the x. 2x + 20 is the perimeter, not the area.)

items.q: Olivia’s poster for the Terry Fox Run is a rectangle with these side lengths in centimetres. Which expression gives its area?
items.e: Area = x(x + 3) = x2 + 3x. (x2 + 3 multiplies only the x. 4x + 6 is the perimeter.)

items.q: A cedar deck in Kelowna is 2x m wide and (x + 5) m long. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
items.e: Area = 2x(x + 5) = 2x2 + 10x. (6x + 10 is the perimeter. 2x2 + 5x forgets to multiply 5 by 2.)

items.q: Ava’s vegetable bed in Nanaimo is (x − 1) m wide and 6 m long. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
items.e: Area = 6(x − 1) = 6x − 6. (6x − 1 multiplies only the x. 2x + 10 is the perimeter.)

items.q: A square patio has sides of 3x m. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
items.e: Area = (3x)(3x) = 9x2. (3x2 squares only the x. 12x is the perimeter.)

items.q: An outdoor hockey rink in Kamloops is 5x m long and (2x + 2) m wide. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
items.e: Area = 5x(2x + 2) = 10x2 + 10x. (10x2 + 2 multiplies only the first term. 14x + 4 is the perimeter.)

items.q: A triangular sail has a base of 4x m and a height of (x + 3) m. Use A = 12bh. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
items.e: 12 × 4x = 2x. Then 2x(x + 3) = 2x2 + 6x. (4x2 + 12x forgets the 12.)

items.q: A parking area at a BC Ferries terminal is 2x m wide and (x + 8) m long. Which expression gives its area in square metres?
items.e: Area = 2x(x + 8) = 2x2 + 16x. (2x2 + 8x multiplies 8 by x but not by 2. 6x + 16 is the perimeter.)

items.q: The deck’s area is (2x2 + 10x) m². What is the area when x = 3?
items.e: Square first: 32 = 9, so 2 × 9 = 18. Then 10 × 3 = 30, and 18 + 30 = 48. The deck is 6 m by 8 m. (66 uses (2 × 3)2. 42 uses 2 × 3 × 2 for 2x2.)

items.q: The rink’s area is (10x2 + 10x) m². What is the area when x = 12?
items.e: 10 × 122 = 10 × 144 = 1440 and 10 × 12 = 120, so the area is 1560 m². The rink is 60 m by 26 m. (172 is the perimeter. 1442 uses 10x2 + 2. 14 520 squares 10 × 12.)

items.q: Sod for a lawn in Burnaby costs $8 per square metre. The lawn’s area is (x2 + 6x) m². Which expression gives the cost in dollars?
items.e: Cost = 8 × area = 8(x2 + 6x) = 8x2 + 48x. (8x2 + 6x multiplies only the first term.)

items.q: The sod costs (8x2 + 48x) dollars. What is the cost when x = 5?
items.e: 8 × 25 = 200 and 48 × 5 = 240, so the cost is $440.00. ($55.00 is only the area in square metres. $230.00 uses 8x2 + 6x.)

items.q: A mural in Vancouver has an area of (12x2 + 18x) m². Its height is 6x m. Which expression gives its length in metres?
items.e: Length = area ÷ height: 12x2 ÷ 6x = 2x and 18x ÷ 6x = 3, so 2x + 3. Check: 6x(2x + 3) = 12x2 + 18x. (2x + 18 divides only the first term. 6x2 + 12x subtracts.)

items.q: A plot at a community garden in Victoria has an area of (5x2 − 10x) m². It is 5x m long. Which expression gives its width in metres?
items.e: Width = area ÷ length: 5x2 ÷ 5x = x and −10x ÷ 5x = −2, so x − 2. (x − 10 divides only the first term.)

items.q: The rectangle has a width of 3x cm. What is its length?
items.e: Length = area ÷ width: 6x2 ÷ 3x = 2x and 9x ÷ 3x = 3, so 2x + 3 cm. (2x + 9 divides only the first term. 3x + 9 subtracts 3x from 6x2.)

items.q: A triangular sign has an area of (3x2 + 6x) cm² and a base of 2x cm. Use A = 12bh. Which expression gives its height in centimetres?
items.e: Double the area to undo the 12: 6x2 + 12x. Then divide by the base 2x: 3x + 6. Check: 12 × 2x × (3x + 6) = 3x2 + 6x. (1.5x + 3 forgets to double the area.)

items.q: A Grade 9 class in Whistler makes 2 rectangular banners for a ski race. Each banner is 3x m long and (x + 2) m wide. Which expression gives the total area of the 2 banners in square metres?
items.e: One banner: 3x(x + 2) = 3x2 + 6x. Two banners: 2(3x2 + 6x) = 6x2 + 12x. (3x2 + 6x is only one banner. 6x2 + 12 drops the x in 6x.)

items.q: Mei’s bedroom floor is (x + 4) m long and 3 m wide. A rug covers 2x m² of it. Which expression gives the area of floor that is not covered?
items.e: Floor area: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12. Subtract the rug: 3x + 12 − 2x = x + 12. (x + 4 forgets to multiply 4 by 3. 5x + 12 adds the rug.)

items.q: Two flower beds are in a park in Prince George. Bed A is x m by (x + 5) m. Bed B is 2x m by 2 m. How much greater is the area of Bed A, in square metres?
items.e: Bed A: x(x + 5) = x2 + 5x. Bed B: 2x × 2 = 4x. Difference: x2 + 5x − 4x = x2 + x. (x2 + 9x adds the areas.)

items.q: Liam puts a square photo with sides of 4x cm on a mat that is 4x cm wide and (4x + 3) cm long. Which expression gives the area of the mat that shows around the photo?
items.e: Mat: 4x(4x + 3) = 16x2 + 12x. Photo: (4x)2 = 16x2. Mat showing: 16x2 + 12x − 16x2 = 12x. (16x2 + 12x forgets to subtract the photo.)
